isa-000nxlg.pub: ISA 000nxlg — Quarantine Lazaret and Infectious Hospital at Haifa
isa-000nxlg.id: ISA 000nxlg · מ-29/4783 · Secretariat C.S. 1/101, P.10734/28 · 6 pp
isa-000nxlg.note:
Six pages of typed correspondence and Secretariat minutes, read in full. It shows that the infectious-diseases block and the quarantine lazaret were conceived as one adjoining project in 1928 — and deferred for cost, a decade before Bat Galim.

The minute of 9 August 1928 states "two admitted needs": enlargement of the Haifa Quarantine Lazaret, and the building of an Infectious Diseases Block, adding that "it is clearly advantageous that the Infectious Diseases Block should adjoin the Lazaret." Land for both was available and approved by a Siting Board — 19 dunum 759 sq m at £P.3175, with the block itself estimated at £P.3970, a total liability of £P.7246 for which there was no provision in the Estimates.

The objection to moving the lazaret to the sand dunes further north is the telling detail: they are "distant from the existing Lazaret and the Railway Station whereas proximity thereto is necessary for the purpose of quarantining of pilgrims or travellers from an infected country." The recommendation was to defer both projects.
isa-000nxlg.pages: pp. 4–6 (Secretariat minutes and the Lands valuation)

isa-000b33x.pub: ISA 000b33x — Quarantine Lazareth Infectious Diseases Hospital, Haifa
isa-000b33x.note:
The expropriation file for the land near the harbour (Shemen beach) taken for the infectious-diseases quarantine station, valued at £P.277.5 per dunum. Includes a letter to Lord Passfield, Colonial Secretary — the same Passfield who issued the 1930 White Paper.

Together with 000nxlg it establishes that the quarantine station and the infectious hospital were a single planning problem for the Mandate government from 1927 to 1934.

isa-0005xx0.pub: ISA 0005xx0 — Government Hospital Haifa, PWD headquarters files
isa-0005xx0.note:
The central construction file: a bundle of Public Works Department headquarters volumes (File No. 1 1935–37, No. 8 1937–39, Vol. 3 1939–42, Vol. 5), 1,569 pages, read in full.

It holds the 1935 bed allocation by section (pp. 323–331: 189 general + 88 fever = 277 beds designed); the 1936 Schedule of Accommodation (pp. 276–289), an eight-page room-by-room list lettered A–V naming every ward block, theatre, store and staff quarter; the St Luke's lease; the September, October and December 1938 handover dates; the 1942 Plague Unit; Solel Boneh as main contractor with the 50/50 Arab-Jewish labour clause and the September 1937 petition alleging it was ignored; and Erich Mendelsohn's copyright claim over the design.

What it does not contain is a ward-labelled plan. Page 1223 is PWD Drawing E/524 of 18 March 1941, a schedule of received record drawings listing about 65 as-built sheets — six storeys, pavilions A–F, a service block — and naming E/R 286 = "KEY PLAN", the sheet that would identify each unit. That sheet is not in the file.
isa-0005xx0.pages: pp. 18 (tender) · 276–289 (schedule of accommodation) · 323–331 (bed allocation) · 727–729 (labour petition) · 1223 (drawings schedule E/524) · 1236–1237 (copyright) · 1301–1421 (plague unit)

isa-000zbri.pub: ISA 000zbri — Monthly Returns, Infectious Diseases, Haifa
isa-000zbri.id: ISA 000zbri · Jan 1942 – Oct 1944 · 388 pp · image only
isa-000zbri.note:
Handwritten monthly returns of notifiable disease for the Haifa district, January 1942 to October 1944. The file is scanned as image only, with no text layer; all 388 pages were rendered and read — 180 nominal pages, 178 daily tallies, 16 blank.

It yields 2,171 named cases and 840 daily tallies for precisely the years the admission registers do not cover, making it the only continuous record for 1942–43. Of the deaths, once measles is excluded, 91% occurred in hospital — the "23% treated at home" figure is almost entirely a measles artefact.

isa-000i5yq.pub: ISA 000i5yq — פנקס המחלות המדבקות, Department of Health, Haifa
isa-000i5yq.note:
A bound nominal register of infectious-disease cases kept by the Haifa Department of Health, December 1921 to December 1928. Each entry names the patient and their parents, their residence, the disease, and the date of recovery or death. Most cases are Haifa residents, with others from Nahalal, Hadera and the surrounding district.

Roughly 7,200 named cases covering the decade before the hospital registers begin. Only partly extracted so far — the largest piece of unworked evidence in the project.

isa-000ucac.pub: ISA 000ucac — New Govt. Hospital Site and Suggested Adjacent Roads
isa-000ucac.note: Town-planning map at 1:2500 by H. Kendall, Town Planning Adviser, showing the site chosen for the new Government Hospital and the roads proposed to serve it. The before image: the shore at Bat Galim as it stood when the building was still a plan.

isa-000w8jb.note: Map at 1:1250 of the completed hospital and its surroundings. The after image to 000ucac's before: the same shore three years on, with the six-storey block and its pavilions in place.

isa-000b0ms.pub: ISA 000b0ms — Site of proposed Government Hospital, Haifa
isa-000b0ms.note: The site file for Bat Galim: the expropriation and purchase of the land beside the monastery, with cadastral plans at 1:2500. Names the owners — Edgar Clark, and the heirs of Fuda Said — and carries the negotiation over price.

isa-0010qhu.pub: ISA 0010qhu — Old Haifa Hospital and Main Disinfecting Station, water supply
isa-0010qhu.note: A water-supply file whose title is itself the finding: "Old Haifa Hospital & Main Disinfecting Station" names the two as one establishment, on Mountain Road, for the whole period before Bat Galim.

isa-00079mb.pub: ISA 00079mb — New Isolation (Fever) Hospital, site selection
isa-00079mb.note: Site selection for a new isolation (fever) hospital. Notes in passing an Infectious Diseases Annex at the Municipal Hospital in 1927 — a third institution in the picture, distinct from both the Government Hospital and the lazaret.

mr-reports.pub: Report by His Majesty's Government on the Administration under Mandate of Palestine and Trans-Jordan
mr-reports.note:
The annual report to the League of Nations, cited here as MR-year with its section number. Scanned by the Internet Archive under the identifiers report-admin-palestine-1928 through -1938; the OCR text is mirrored in the project as sources/archives/mandate-reports/t<year>.txt.

These are the Mandate government's own account of what it built and spent. The link opens the 1928 volume; change the year in the address for the others.

jem-cat.pub: Jerusalem and the East Mission archive, catalogue GB165-0161
jem-cat.place: Middle East Centre Archive, St Antony's College, Oxford
jem-cat.note:
The catalogue of the Jerusalem & the East Mission papers, the Anglican body that ran St Luke's Hospital in Haifa until 1929. Cited here as JEM-cat; the catalogue text is mirrored in the project as sources/archives/meca-jem-catalogue.txt.

It holds box 119/1, "Correspondence re: St Luke's property, Haifa, 1933–1937" — the mission's deliberation over disposing of the building after the hospital closed. It also corrects a citation: Mahmoud gives the 1928–29 annual report as Box 75a/2, but 75A/2 holds volumes 3–4 (1903–1915); the 1926–1930 reports are volume 7, in 75B/2.
